notes: Company overview: mid-market SaaS (B2B) — multi-tenant customer support platform; strong PLG motion; product teams want conversational agents embedded in web app.
Contacts: Rajiv Sharma (CTO), Elena Wu (Head of Product), Nora Kim (Sr. Eng, infra). AE intro = Maya Patel; SE = Carlos Mendes.
Initial ask: hosted API trial now, Dedicated if hosted can't meet latency/throughput SLOs or cost targets. They want clear path to Dedicated with minimal code changes.
Primary workload: real-time support chat agents (web + mobile). Must support streaming responses and tool-calling for real-time actions (ticket lookup, order status).
Latency SLO: target first-token <1.5s p95 on typical EU/NA traffic. Want streaming with sub-200ms token increments for perceived responsiveness.
Throughput: peak 60 concurrent agents per region for current customer base; expect growth x3 in 12 months. Autoscaling + burst capacity important.

Model preferences: open to curated open models for cost control (quantized variants), but will compare Redwood-verified models vs OpenAI baseline. Concern: hallucination rate on tool outputs must be low.
Security: must have SSO/SAML for admin console, audit logs, KMS integration for customer secrets, retention controls for transcripts (30–90 days depending customer). Legal asked for SOC2 evidence.

POC plan agreed 2026-03-15: 2-week POC using hosted API. POC checklist: set up streaming chat, implement tool-calling webhook, measure p50/p95 first-token latency, run regression evals on prompt sets.
Pricing: finance asked for estimated committed capacity pricing vs pay-as-you-go. Interested in ded. pricing for 3–6 month reserve if POC meets SLA.
Notes from last call (2026-02-18 ff_2026-02-18_01): 'if we can hit <1.5s p95 with streaming + tools, we'll move to pilot with 2 key customers' (Elena).
Technical constraints: current infra on GCP in us-east1 and europe-west1. Prefer Redwood routing to keep EU traffic local. Wants transparent token-level cost breakdown in console.
Decisions to make: acceptable fallback model if primary variant under capacity; how to route between hosted->dedicated during rollout; KV cache strategy for tickets.
Competitive notes: currently using OpenAI for prototypes — price OK but want predictable latency + dedicated capacity option. Team evaluated Anthropic on safety but cost too high at scale.
Next technical action (SE): create sample streaming integration with tool-calls to their ticketing API; capture metrics and share dashboard before 2026-03-22.
Sales action: provide committed-capacity pricing scenarios (3/6/12 mo) and migration checklist from hosted to Dedicated. Include SLA targets and runbook for fallback.
Quote/fragments from Rajiv: 'We cannot compromise on perceived snappiness — first token is everything for chat UX.'
POC success criteria: p95 first-token <1.5s, tool-call latency <250ms (end-to-end), model quality pass on 90% of 200 eval prompts, and cost per active conversation within forecasted ARR targets.
Risks: if hosted API can't hit SLOs at scale, Dedicated procurement cycle could push close to late Q3. Legal timeline for SOC2 proof may delay procurement.
Internal follow-ups: sync with infra team about routing rules and cold-start mitigation; capture kernel/quantization recommendations from Optimize team.
